summary: Streaming chat connection unexpectedly cuts mid-response correlated with TLS rekey/renegotiation
description: Issue summary: Customer reports streaming chat sessions (SSE and WebSocket) terminating silently in the middle of a long generated message. Impact: multiple users at ClearLedger observing final 20-60% of responses missing; visible as client-side 'stream closed' with no error token. Environment: production API gateway fronted by AWS ALB, nginx sidecars, serving-runtime pool with GPU workers. Observed after ~2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Time window: intermittent but reproducible for the customer on weekdays during their business hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ClearLedger app or run: curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.stream -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Generate a 1200 word analysis of quarterly results"}]}'
2) Observe initial token stream for ~15-30s then an abrupt connection close without final event or [DONE] marker
3) Repeat behind a corporate proxy with TLS inspection (if available) to reproduce renego behavior
4) Capture tcpdump on client and gateway to inspect TLS handshake around disconnect timestamp
logs: Gateway logs show 200 responses with streaming connection established, then TCP FIN from upstream at byte offset ~16384 or shortly after. Nginx access: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream. Kernel: tcp_close_xmit around same timestamp on worker node ip-10-1-*. ClearLedger supplied packet capture shows a TLS ClientHello at disconnect time that appears to be a renegotiation/rekey event. No 5xx returned to client. Serving-runtime logs show worker completed generation but final flush to socket returned EPIPE.
investigation: Initial hypothesis: mid-stream TLS rekey/renegotiation initiated by corporate network appliance or client causes upstream connection to be reset while runtime still streaming. Evidence: (1) packet capture from customer shows TLS handshake 'rekey' shortly before FIN, (2) repeated reproductions when client uses TLS 1.2 with certain cipher suites, (3) no runtime exception before EPIPE on socket write. Reproduced internally by configuring a test client to force TLS renegotiation after ~14-18s of streaming; this consistently triggers streaming termination without graceful SSE [DONE] marker. Correlated with ALB idle timeout being 60s but our observed close occurs earlier at rekey. Root cause candidate: some middleboxes/clients treat TLS rekey/renegotiation as connection restart rather than in-band key update, causing upstream to drop the TCP stream while the server attempts further writes. Alternate contributing factor: our streaming keepalive cadence is 30s by default; when rekey occurs earlier there is a window with no heartbeat.
comments: Support (Maya): Customer reported ~12 users seeing truncated responses in production, provided pcap and timestamps. Initial asking for runbook and possible workarounds.
SRE (Amir): Confirmed pcap shows TLS ClientHello/ServerHello exchange at ~15s into stream. Worker attempted write and got EPIPE. Reproduced locally with openssl s_client forcing renegotiation.
Customer (ClearLedger): We maintain a corporate TLS inspection appliance (BlueProxy) that sometimes triggers rekey on long-lived connections. Can you recommend a workaround?
SRE (Amir): Short-term workaround: reduce streaming heartbeat interval to 10s and disable nginx proxy buffering for affected route. We will also test ALB/NLB config and server-side keepalives.

Eng (Priya Rao): Opened runtime PR to flush small heartbeat comments every 10s and to guard writes against EPIPE by continuing generation into a fallback buffer then terminating gracefully if connection gone. See PR #4872.

Support (Maya): Customer applied client-side bypass (disable deep packet inspection for our endpoint) and confirmed immediate improvement; ClearLedger requests official mitigation from Redwood so they don't have to reconfigure their appliance.
root_cause: In-production TLS rekey/renegotiation triggered by intermediate TLS-inspecting appliances or client stacks caused the TCP connection to be treated as restarted; the serving runtime continued to stream and hit EPIPE which resulted in silent mid-response truncation. Lack of aggressive keepalive/heartbeat shortly before the rekey increased the chance of an unobserved disconnect.
resolution: Rolled out a two-part mitigation on 2026-03-11: (1) API gateway config change to set nginx proxy_buffering off for streaming routes and set proxy_read_timeout to 120s; (2) runtime change (PR #4872) to emit a lightweight SSE comment keepalive every 10s and to detect EPIPE more gracefully and mark stream as 'aborted' with a final error event when possible. Deployed to us-east prod canary then full cluster at 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC. Customer confirmed restores full responses. A follow-up action was scheduled to add telemetry to count TLS rekey events and client cipher suites.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add telemetry in gateway for TLS session update/ClientHello events and correlate with stream aborts
2) Update public streaming runbook to recommend shorter keepalive and guidance for enterprise customers with TLS inspection appliances
3) Add test harness that injects TLS renegotiation during streaming to catch regressions in CI
4) Customer outreach: notify enterprise customers with known TLS inspection deployments about recommended config
5) Consider altering default heartbeat from 30s to 10s for streaming endpoints behind ALBs in next minor release
final_notes: Status: Resolved for ClearLedger in us-east after config + runtime mitigations. Monitoring in place to detect similar pattern in other regions. If customers still see truncations, ask for packet capture and whether corporate TLS inspection is in path.
